NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks stack voltage and coolant temperature. My observable is the local electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) phase angle at high frequency (1-10 kHz), which reflects the membrane's hydration state without additional sensors.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
The observable can be computed from existing voltage and current sensors using standard Fourier transform analysis at the existing sampling rate (≥10 kHz).

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks global stack voltage and temperature as proxies for membrane health. My observable, local high-frequency EIS phase angle, directly measures the membrane's ionic resistance distribution by detecting the capacitive-reactive component of the membrane-electrode interface, which is sensitive to hydration state changes before they manifest as voltage drops or temperature anomalies.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing relation is Z = R + j/(2πfC), where Z is impedance, R is resistance, f is frequency, and C is capacitance. The phase angle φ = arctan(1/(2πfRC)) shifts as membrane hydration changes C. At 5 kHz and typical membrane values (R ≈ 0.15 Ω·cm², C ≈ 0.3 F/cm²), φ ≈ 21°. A 10% hydration decrease reduces C by ~15%, causing φ to shift by ~3°, detectable above measurement noise.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
1. Software module for real-time FFT analysis of voltage/current ripple (existing sensors)
2. Bandpass filter (1-10 kHz) - off-the-shelf digital filter implementation
3. Phase angle calculation algorithm - standard signal processing library
4. Local impedance mapping - existing cell voltage resolution (≥10 mV)
5. Processing unit - existing stack controller (no new hardware required)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: SAME - no new hardware installation
- Operability: SAME - uses existing control system interface
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance points
- Cost class: SAME - software-only implementation
- Data storage: MODERATE increase (~5%) for phase angle maps
- Computational load: MINOR increase (FFT processing)

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Operate stack at 1.5 A/cm² and 80°C while gradually reducing cathode humidity from 100% to 30% RH. Record phase angle maps every 5 minutes until failure occurs.
Instruments: Existing stack monitoring system with data logging capability.
Pass/fail threshold: Failure is defined when phase angle deviation from baseline exceeds 5° in any cell or stack power output drops by >5%.
Duration: Test until failure or 8 hours, whichever comes first.
Kill criterion: Immediate shutdown if any cell temperature exceeds 90°C or voltage drops below 0.5V.
